kind: Building-edge visibility regression, not an FPS benchmark
cause: The grid-cell tile region is smaller than its own declared content region. Cesium rejects the tile before testing the larger building content volume.
correction: Enclose valid geographic tile regions around their declared content and child regions without changing model geometry.
Propagate late external root extents through existing ancestor headers and cached Cesium bounding volumes; invalidate the affected visibility cache.
Retain bounds repair when the local-header memory cap requires unsplit loading.
Retain source content bounds, transforms, payloads, camera FOV, graphics-profile settings and ordinary offscreen culling.

renderingCheck.platform: Windows, actual Cesium 1.145.0 in headless Chrome with D3D11 requested
renderingCheck.method: Load the actual official hall tile first, isolate it from other buildings, then toggle its original/corrected region at identical poses using the flight camera adapter. Terrain, imagery, payload and materials remain the same.
renderingCheck.visualResult: Local renderer screenshots inspected: roof/wall fragments visible at the edge and lower foreground reappear with the corrected region.

offlineRegressionChecks.result: No content-region intersection is rejected by the corrected tile or parent region in these samples; the original headers reproduce more than 100 premature rejections.
offlineRegressionChecks.offscreenControl: 360 upward-looking headings verify that normal offscreen culling remains active.
otherCoverage: Late external ancestors through an unchanged intermediate tile
Unchanged content bounds and payload URLs
One-byte test header budget exercising the memory fallback

limits: One original-model location and five paired rendering views; this is not an exhaustive dataset-wide visual check.
The rendering comparison preceded the final memory-fallback addition, which is covered separately by the offline regression test; the rendering run remained below the default header budget.
Repair uses valid non-wrapping geographic region bounds. Unsupported box, sphere, implicit, invalid and wrapping volumes retain their existing handling.
No physical Android or native Windows WebView2 frame-rate or memory claim is made.
Original imagery, building payloads and local screenshots are not included in the code archive.
